title: Transcriptomic classifier shows limited cross-dataset Long COVID discrimination
summary: A bioRxiv preprint from the Institute of Bioinformatics and collaborators analyzes six RNA-sequencing datasets from Long COVID and recovered patients. Its primary abstract reports mean AUC0.664 for an RBF support-vector classifier across six leave-one-batch-out folds. Gene hypotheses were derived from three selected higher-performing folds and then used for pathway and interaction analyses; these do not establish causal mechanisms, effective drugs or clinical utility. This review covers the primary abstract and metadata; full-text HTML and PDF access were blocked.
organization: Institute of Bioinformatics, Bangalore; Indian Council of Medical Research; University of Delhi

evidence.tested: Retrospective leave-one-batch-out discrimination across six transcriptomic datasets, mean AUC0.664; SHAP-derived features from three selected folds support hypothesis generation.
evidence.unknown: Full methods, patient counts, leakage controls and batch-specific performance were not assessed because full-text routes were inaccessible. Experimental mechanisms, drug benefit and clinical utility are not established.
evidence.ai_role: The learned RBF support-vector classifier distinguishes Long COVID from recovered-patient transcriptomic profiles across held-out batches; SHAP nominates features for further analyses.

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 abstract, author affiliations and posted date; full HTML/PDF routes returned403 and were not reviewed
